newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco says will not renew EU fishing accord.
newsitem.headline: Morocco says will not renew EU fishing accord.

text.p: Morocco said on Saturday it would not renew its three-year fishing accord with the European Union allowing a fleet of 700 vessels to fish in Moroccan waters.
"The Moroccan government has decided not to renew the three-year fishing accord signed with the European Union earlier this year," a Moroccan official at the fisheries ministry said.
But he said Morocco remained "open to other forms of partnership and cooperation in the fishing sector".
The accord, initialled in November 1995 after months of wrangling, was finally signed in Brussels in February 1996.
It sets out all the principles, rules and details of fisheries cooperation between Brussels and Rabat, particulary prevention of overfishing and the sale of fish once caught.
The cost to the EU was set at the equivalent of $600 million between 1996 and the end of 1999.
The Moroccan government's decision was aimed at protecting the country's fish resources and stocks, the official said.
